description: Instruction selection decomposed. Map IR operations to target ISA instructions. Tree pattern matching, DAG pattern matching, BURS (bottom-up rewriting system), peephole optimisation, target description languages (LLVM TableGen, GCC machine description). LLVM's SelectionDAG architecture.

sub_mechanisms.name: instruction_pattern
sub_mechanisms.definition: Description of an ISA instruction's behaviour as an IR sub-tree pattern. Match the pattern → emit the instruction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bridges IR's abstract operations to ISA's concrete ones. Each instruction has 1+ patterns. Patterns include cost (cycle count, code size) for optimal selection.

sub_mechanisms.name: tree_pattern_matching
sub_mechanisms.definition: Match IR tree against patterns. Each pattern is a tree fragment; matched node emits the corresponding instruction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tree matching is well-studied (BURS, Aho-Sethi). Handles simple cases like 'add r1, r2, r3' but breaks when IR isn't strictly tree-shaped (shared subexpressions).

sub_mechanisms.name: DAG_pattern_matching
sub_mechanisms.definition: Generalisation to DAGs (common in IR after CSE). Each node may match multiple patterns; combination must be consistent.
sub_mechanisms.why: IR after optimisation typically has shared sub-expressions (CSE). DAG matching handles this without splitting back to trees. More complex than tree matching but matches reality.

sub_mechanisms.name: BURS
sub_mechanisms.definition: Bottom-Up Rewriting System: dynamic programming over the IR DAG. At each node, compute min-cost cover among matching patterns.
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimal tiling for the DAG with given pattern costs. Classical technique (Aho-Sethi 1989). LLVM's SelectionDAG ISel is BURS-based.

sub_mechanisms.name: LLVM_SelectionDAG
sub_mechanisms.definition: LLVM's IR → MachineInstr converter. Per-function DAG; nodes are IR ops; rules from TableGen .td files match against the DAG.
sub_mechanisms.why: Production instruction selector. Each backend (X86, ARM, RISCV) provides patterns via TableGen; the framework handles common matching infrastructure. Standard since LLVM 2.x.

sub_mechanisms.name: LLVM_GlobalISel
sub_mechanisms.definition: Replacement for SelectionDAG. Operates on whole function, eliminates per-basic-block boundary issues, faster compile times.
sub_mechanisms.why: SelectionDAG operates per-block, missing cross-block opportunities. GlobalISel works globally. Gradually replacing SelectionDAG in LLVM; ARM64 has been a leader in adopting it.

sub_mechanisms.name: peephole_optimisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Local optimisation after instruction selection. Scan small windows of instructions for known patterns; rewrite.
sub_mechanisms.why: Catches cases instruction selection missed or introduced. e.g., (mov a, r; add a, b) → (lea r + b, a). Used by every production compiler. Simple, fast, robust.

sub_mechanisms.name: TableGen
sub_mechanisms.definition: LLVM's domain-specific language for describing targets. .td files declare registers, instructions, calling conventions, patterns.
sub_mechanisms.why: Declarative target description. LLVM generates code (decoders, encoders, pattern matchers) from .td files. New target = mostly TableGen + some C++.

sub_mechanisms.name: GCC_machine_description
sub_mechanisms.definition: GCC's analogous DSL: .md files describe instructions as RTL templates. The pattern matcher reads them.
sub_mechanisms.why: GCC's analogue of TableGen, predating it. Each backend describes itself via .md. Older + less polished than TableGen but powers the same kind of automatic backend generation.

sub_mechanisms.name: tile_cost_model
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each instruction pattern has a cost: cycles, code size, latency. ISel picks minimum-cost cover.
sub_mechanisms.why: Multiple ways to express IR op as ISA instructions. Cost model chooses best. x86's LEA can implement add + shift in one instruction at lower cost than separate instructions.

sub_mechanisms.name: addressing_mode_matching
sub_mechanisms.definition: x86 addressing modes (base + index*scale + offset) match complex IR patterns. ISel folds address computation into a single memory access.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without folding, 'load (a + b*4 + 8)' becomes 4 instructions. With folding: 1 LEA + 1 load (or 1 load with addressing mode). Major code density + performance win.

sub_mechanisms.name: instruction_legalisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pre-ISel pass converting IR ops the target doesn't support directly. e.g., i128 add on x86 → two i64 adds + carry.
sub_mechanisms.why: IR is target-independent; many ops aren't directly supported. Legalisation makes the IR target-feasible before ISel. Specific to each target's capabilities.

derivation_rules.name: BURS_optimal_for_tree_or_DAG_matching
derivation_rules.why: Dynamic programming optimal: each subtree's min cost computed from its children's. Provably optimal among the given patterns. Cost accuracy determines quality; LLVM's costs are approximate but well-tuned.

derivation_rules.name: addressing_mode_folding_dominates_code_density
if: target ISA has rich addressing modes (x86)
then: folding address computation into memory ops dramatically improves code density
derivation_rules.why: x86's [base + index*scale + offset] saves 2-3 explicit ALU instructions per memory access. Code size + execution time both improve. ISel's address-mode matching is one of the highest-impact opportunities.

derivation_rules.name: DAG_matching_required_after_CSE
then: tree matching fails; DAG matching is required
derivation_rules.why: CSE produces shared nodes (one expression with multiple uses). Tree matching would duplicate; DAG matching reuses. Real IR is DAG-shaped after optimisation; tree-only matchers are obsolete.

derivation_rules.name: TableGen_declarative_description_amortises_target_work
then: framework generates most of the backend
derivation_rules.why: Decoder, encoder, pattern matcher, asm printer all generated from .td files. Adding new architecture: weeks of TableGen vs months of hand-written code. Foundation of LLVM's target proliferation.

derivation_rules.name: peephole_complements_global_isel
derivation_rules.why: Global ISel optimises structure but may produce sub-optimal local patterns. Peephole's small window catches these cheaply. Standard pipeline: global ISel + RA + scheduling + peephole.
